# Temple Scroll Column 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 30 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**30:1** Build an outer court. Along the south side, it shall stretch one thousand six hundred cubits from corner to corner.

**30:2** The south wall runs from the southeastern corner westward to the southwestern corner.

**30:3** Place three gates along the south wall, equally spaced from each other and from the corners.

**30:4** Each gate shall be forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits tall to the lintel.

**30:5** Before each gate, build an entrance hall forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits deep, with watchtowers rising above.

**30:6** The east side of the outer court shall also stretch one thousand six hundred cubits from corner to corner.

**30:7** The east wall runs from the southeastern corner northward to the northeastern corner.

**30:8** Place three gates along the east wall, equally spaced from each other and from the corners.

**30:9** These gates shall match the same dimensions: forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits high.

**30:10** Each gate shall have an identical entrance hall, with watchtowers above.

**30:11** The north side extends one thousand six hundred cubits, running from the northeastern corner westward to the northwestern corner.

**30:12** Place three gates along the north wall, equally spaced, with the same dimensions as the others.

**30:13** The west side extends one thousand six hundred cubits, from the northwestern corner southward to the southwestern corner.

**30:14** Place three gates along the west wall, equally spaced, matching the same dimensions.

**30:15** The total perimeter of the outer court is six thousand four hundred cubits — a massive square measured from corner to corner.

**30:16** Build the outer court wall seven cubits thick and forty-nine cubits high, on a foundation of cut stone sunk three cubits into the ground.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 30 well preserved. The outer court is staggeringly large — approximately 730 meters (nearly half a mile) per side, dwarfing any temple ever built. The twelve gates (three per side) clearly correspond to the twelve tribes of Israel. The wall height of forty-nine cubits (seven times seven) reflects the scroll's fascination with the number seven. "Watchtowers" used for the gate towers to convey their defensive and surveillance function.*
